evals.prompt: I need to read the agent ID assigned to my runtime installation from within the agentware SDK. The agent was set up in the Kei console and attached to the installation. How do I get the agent ID in TypeScript, and what should I do if identity is not available?
evals.expected_output: Uses link.identity() from @haikeilabs/agentware >= 0.4.0 with kei-proxy >= 0.1.11, reads defaultAgentId and agents from the identity object, denies governed calls if identity is unavailable rather than guessing a fallback agent ID.
expectations: The response reads agent identity from link.identity(), not from an environment variable.
The response denies governed calls when identity is undefined rather than guessing a fallback agent ID.
The response requires kei-proxy >= 0.1.11 and agentware >= 0.4.0.

evals.prompt: I'm writing a custom harness in Python and need to govern my agents' tool calls through Kei. Show me how to construct a KeiProxyEvaluator and what happens when kei-proxy is unreachable.
evals.expected_output: Builds the client with select_authorization_client (the kei-proxy serve socket client when KEI_RUNTIME_SOCKET_PATH is set, else the KeiProxyAuthorizeClient CLI fallback), wraps it in KeiProxyEvaluator, explains that an unreachable proxy yields DENY with proxy_unavailable reason (fail-closed), and uses evaluator.evaluate() before every tool call.
expectations: constructs KeiProxyEvaluator over the client from select_authorization_client
explains that an unreachable proxy denies with proxy_unavailable (fail-closed)
calls evaluator.evaluate() before each tool call with tool name, args, and caller context

checks.text: constructs KeiProxyEvaluator over the client from select_authorization_client
explains that an unreachable proxy denies with proxy_unavailable (fail-closed)
calls evaluator.evaluate() before each tool call with tool name, args, and caller context

evals.prompt: My Python agent harness will run in a container next to `kei-proxy serve`. How should it connect to kei-proxy for tool authorization, and what does it have to do before it starts serving requests?
evals.expected_output: Uses the agentware socket client: sync the tool manifest first with sync_tool_manifest (ToolManifestSyncConfig.from_env), which refuses an empty manifest and must stop the harness from serving on failure; then select_authorization_client with KEI_RUNTIME_SOCKET_PATH set so the socket client (KeiProxySocketAuthorizeClient, sessions via open_session) is used; wrap it in KeiProxyEvaluator. Imports from haikeilabs.agentware.kei (pedro_agentware.kei is a deprecated shim). The kei-proxy authorize CLI is only the fallback when no daemon runs.
expectations: syncs the tool manifest with sync_tool_manifest before serving
selects the socket client with select_authorization_client and KEI_RUNTIME_SOCKET_PATH
says an empty manifest is refused
keeps the kei-proxy authorize CLI only as the fallback when no daemon runs

checks.text: syncs the tool manifest with sync_tool_manifest before serving
selects the socket client with select_authorization_client and KEI_RUNTIME_SOCKET_PATH
says an empty manifest is refused
keeps the kei-proxy authorize CLI only as the fallback when no daemon runs

evals.prompt: Our Go harness sets KEI_RUNTIME_SOCKET_PATH, but the kei-proxy daemon is down. Should the harness quietly fall back to spawning `kei-proxy authorize` so tools keep working? Also, can we log the KEI_RUNTIME_TOKEN at debug level to troubleshoot?
evals.expected_output: No. runtimesocket.SelectAuthorizationClient chooses once: a configured socket that is down is a refusal (proxy_unavailable), never a silent fall back to the CLI; KeiProxyEvaluator denies (fail-closed). The runtime token is never logged: it is sent only as Authorization: Bearer and never appears in a log line, an error or String().
expectations: says a configured socket that is down is a refusal with proxy_unavailable
says there is no fall back to the CLI
says the runtime token is never logged
names the Go selector runtimesocket.SelectAuthorizationClient
